content: 1. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of alprazolam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction requires close monitoring and caution, as ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to elevated serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. 2. Ambrisentan can increase the levels or effects of etonogestrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Ethinylestradiol, when used with aminocaproic acid, may result in additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Ethinylestradiol may interact with amitriptyline through an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) effects while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 5. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Amoxicillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ampicillin has a similar interaction with ethinylestradiol as amoxicillin, decreasing its levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This also applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 8. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Additionally, anastrozole may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unknown. 9. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of antipyrine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 10. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can lead to reduced efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Women of reproductive potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 11. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 12. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of asenapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 15. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 17. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 19. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Women of reproductive potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 20. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Bendamustine is metabolized to minimally active metabolites by CYP1A2, and concurrent administration may increase plasma concentrations. Monitoring is recommended. 21. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 22. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can lead to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Women should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 23. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 24. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 25. Calaspargase pegol may interact indirectly with oral contraceptives, potentially reducing their efficacy. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for women of childbearing potential. 26. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, and alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 27. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime) may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 28. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use additional or alternative non-hormonal contraception during concomitant use with oral contraceptives. 29. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 30. Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 32. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 33. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 34. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 35. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 36. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 37. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction requires close monitoring and caution, as ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to elevated serum concentrations. 38. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered.
